items.description:
In this episode of Just Ride, Rob Warner and Eliot Jackson sit down with Neko Mulally to talk about building Frameworks Racing from the ground up, from homemade bike prototypes to one of the most talked-about teams in downhill mountain biking.

Neko shares the story behind signing Asa Vermette, bringing Aaron Gwin onto the team, developing World Cup race bikes, and creating a team culture built around trust, performance, and progression. The conversation dives into bike setup, rider development, Hardline, American downhill racing, and what it really takes to compete at the highest level.

They also discuss the future of Frameworks, growing the sport in the U.S., and why simplicity, confidence, and passion still matter in modern downhill MTB.

items.title: 14 Years In The Making 🥇 | THE B LINE 🇫🇷 | WHOOP UCI MTB World Series
items.description:
A blockbuster weekend in the French Pyrenees saw the world's fastest downhill riders take on the legendary slopes of Loudenvielle-Peyragudes. From long-awaited breakthroughs to emotional returns to the top step, Round 2 of the UCI Downhill World Cup delivered unforgettable moments from start to finish.

Join Ashleigh Wilmot as she breaks down the biggest stories from the weekend, including Vali Höll's return to winning ways, Luca Shaw's long-awaited first UCI Downhill World Cup victory, and Lisa Baumann securing the first Elite World Cup podium of her career.

We'll also dive into some of the best stories from the pits and paddock, getting to know the personalities behind the helmets and exploring life off the bike during a busy World Cup weekend.

items.title: Gracey Hemstreet & Asa Vermette Take On Loudenvielle – The Setup | FOX
items.description:
Last season, Loudenvielle delivered one of the standout moments of the year. On a track known for its steep gradients, and flat out motorways, Gracey Hemstreet put together a breakthrough performance to claim her first Elite World Cup victory. Carrying that confidence through the rest of the season, she went on to add two more wins and establish herself as one of the fastest riders in the field.
 
The 2026 season has already produced another breakthrough story. In South Korea, Asa Vermette made an unforgettable Elite debut, taking victory in his very first World Cup start and joining a select group of riders to achieve that feat.
 
Now the series returns to Loudenvielle for Round 2 of the UCI Downhill World Cup. With it's demanding mix of wild steeps, bike park terrain, and relentless pace, the French venue remains one of the toughest tests on the calendar.
 
This week, we're going behind the scenes with Gracey, Asa, and their respective teams and FOX to see what it takes to prepare for finals day. From track walks and bike setup to race-day routines and last-minute adjustments, get an inside look at how some of the world's top riders get ready to perform when it boils down to race day. 
 
Host: Remi Gauvin 
Video: Brooks Curran 
 
#FOX #RideFox #TheSetup

items.title: The Team NOBODY Saw Coming | Neko Mullaly on Finding Asa Vermette and Building Frameworks
items.description:
In this episode of Just Ride, Rob Warner and Eliot Jackson sit down with Neko Mulally to talk about building Frameworks Racing from the ground up, from homemade bike prototypes to one of the most talked-about teams in downhill mountain biking.

Neko shares the story behind signing Asa Vermette, bringing Aaron Gwin onto the team, developing World Cup race bikes, and creating a team culture built around trust, performance, and progression. The conversation dives into bike setup, rider development, Hardline, American downhill racing, and what it really takes to compete at the highest level.

They also discuss the future of Frameworks, growing the sport in the U.S., and why simplicity, confidence, and passion still matter in modern downhill MTB.

Looking for more Just Ride? Check out all the episodes here:

items.title: Frameworks 32-Inch-Wheeled DH Bike EXPLAINED
items.description: Neko Mulally is tested out a 32" front wheel on his downhill bike at the  @prodownhillseries  at Mountain Creek. He's running a custom-made FOX 40 fork that's been extended to fit the wheel along with a custom frame to help sort out geometry and axle-to-crown height. His rear wheel remains 27.5".
